essence: The Aglaura built from what its people always say about it is solid and complete, while the Aglaura that actually stands on the ground is faded and random and, having no words of its own, slips out of memory.
textDetails: What Marco can report is mostly what the inhabitants themselves keep repeating: a stock of proverbial virtues, matching proverbial faults, a handful of oddities and a fussy deference to rules.
Old-time observers, presumed reliable, assigned Aglaura this durable mix of qualities, presumably by measuring it against other cities of their era.
Neither the described city nor the visible one may have changed much since; what shifted is the scale of judgement: former eccentricities now count as normal, and former norms now look odd.
Its virtues and faults no longer earn praise or shame, because the whole set of qualities has been redistributed (Weaver calls it a 'code'; the Italian word is 'concerto').
So none of the sayings about Aglaura is true, and yet together they produce a firm, compact picture of a city, while the loose impressions gathered by living there are flimsier.
The talked-about city therefore has more of what existence requires than the city physically occupying the spot, which exists to a lesser degree.
Judged only by Marco's own eyes, Aglaura would be washed-out and colourless, lacking character, placed there haphazardly.
Even that is false: at particular hours and from particular angles down a street, there is a sudden suspicion of something rare and unmistakable, possibly splendid.
The moment you try to put it into words, the accumulated sayings about Aglaura take over your sentence, and you end up echoing instead of describing.
Hence the residents think they inhabit an Aglaura sustained purely by its name, and overlook the Aglaura actually growing out of the soil.
Marco himself can speak only of the first; the second, never fixed in words, has faded from his memory (the Italian says it has dispersed).

Design note: the text names no buildings, materials, colours or numbers; its only physical qualities are faded, characterless and randomly placed, plus the fleeting glimpses. All architecture in this brief is invented to stage the idea.
visualConcept: A floating disc of pale ash-coloured earth carries two Aglauras, one hovering over the other and never touching it. On the ground lies the Aglaura rooted in the earth: a sprawl of low, faded, characterless blocks dropped at random, with random rotations, accidental crooked lanes and no landmark, rendered desaturated and dithered to about 70 percent opacity so the fog passes through it (it literally exists less). Above it floats the Aglaura that grows on the name: a compact, symmetrical, gilt-ivory citadel whose only foundation is a ring of seven monumental letters, A-G-L-A-U-R-A, standing like pillars in mid-air, so that as the camera circles, the name reads round and round without end; think of the model city a patron saint holds in an old altarpiece. The upper city is lit by its own warm, low sun that never reaches the ground, its walls are banded with rows of tiny engraved glyphs repeated endlessly (the proverbs everyone recites), and it keeps a few official eccentricities, one leaning tower and one inverted dome, as part of its fixed image; in the sprawl below, by contrast, leaning is common and the one perfectly regular house is the oddity. The upper city turns very slowly, so its avenues never line up with the streets beneath. Over the grey sprawl a single soft break in the overcast wanders, and wherever it rests a narrow slit of light can open onto something rare: a fragment of iridescent, impossibly coloured architecture, with colour flooding back into the neighbouring houses. Before it can be grasped, ribbons of gilt glyphs uncoil from the name-city, cage the vision and press it into one more copy of the stock gilt house, which greys and dissolves. At a glance: the said city is heavy, golden and certain; the lived city is pale, real and unsayable.
layout: Floating disc of earth, radius 22, top at y=0, 2.5 thick, with a ragged underside tapering into fog. Ground city: 260-320 instanced blocks scattered by plain uniform random (deliberately clumpy, with accidental gaps that read as crooked lanes), footprints 0.6-2.0 by 0.6-1.6, heights 0.4-1.8 with a few at 2.5, random yaw, about a third leaning 3-8 degrees; exactly one perfectly regular gabled house, identical to the upper city's stock house, sits among them as the oddity; about 40 tiny people (0.25 tall) on random walks. Name ring: seven upright letters A G L A U R A on a circle of radius 8.5, evenly spaced (about 51.4 degrees apart), facing outward, each 3.2 tall, 2.2 wide and 0.7 deep, built procedurally from extruded box strokes and arcs (only A, G, L, U and R are needed), bottoms at y=3.2 (clear of the tallest roof), tops at y=6.4. Upper city: a disc of radius 10 and 0.8 thick resting on the letters (y 6.4 to 7.2); crenellated outer wall at r=9.6, 1.2 tall, with 7 round towers 3 tall standing directly above the 7 letters; three terraces stepping up 0.9 each at r=8, 6 and 4, packed with about 220 identical instanced houses in exact concentric rows; 7 radial avenues aligned with the letters; a central domed tower 6 tall with a lantern (top near y=15.5); one tower leaning 7 degrees and one small dome set upside down. The wandering light-break is a soft pool of radius 4 drifting over the ground city on a slow random path; glimpses can open at any lane point inside it.
signatureMotion: 1) Glimpse and capture, every 7-11 s: inside the wandering pool of light, a vertical slit of white light opens in a lane (0.1 to 1.4 wide, 2.5 tall, over 1 s) and reveals one of five iridescent marvels (a spiral stair climbing into nothing, a cluster of faceted glass domes, a receding arcade of nested arches, a hanging garden of luminous leaves, a stack of floating rings) in a thin-film shader shifting through teal, rose and gold, while a saturation bubble of radius 3 restores colour to the surrounding houses; after 2.5 s, 6-8 gilt ribbons printed with tiny repeated glyphs (a canvas-drawn texture) spiral down from the underside of the upper city, close round the marvel like the bars of a lantern-cage, drain its colour to gold and squeeze it into a small copy of the stock gilt house, which greys and dissolves (about 6 s in all). 2) The upper city and its ring of letters revolve slowly (one turn per 4 minutes) above the motionless ground city, while the engraved glyph bands scroll along its walls like proverbs being recited. 3) Dust and pale fog drift straight through the semi-transparent ground houses, whose opacity flickers faintly, as if they were not quite there.
interactionDescription: Shifts attention from the name to the ground. The upper city drains to a pale gold outline, its letter-pillars thin to wireframe, its private sun fades, and the camera eases down toward the rooftops of the grey sprawl. The ground houses firm up to full opacity and pick up faint individual tints while you look, and glimpses open twice as often and more fully; no ribbons come to cage them, but each marvel simply breaks into coloured motes that thin into the fog and leave nothing behind, because there are no words to fix it. Toggle off and the name-city snaps back to solid gold, the tints drain away, and the glimpses are caged again.
mood: An overcast, sourceless late afternoon: flat milky light on the ground city, almost no shadows, dust and pale fog pooling in the lanes and thinning with height. The upper city alone is lit by a low warm sun from nowhere, crisp as an engraving, as if illuminated by old reports rather than by the sky. Quiet, slightly stale air; the only true colour arrives in the brief glimpses.
caption: Ask in Aglaura and you will hear the same virtues, the same faults, the same small manias, recited exactly as the grandparents recited them. From those sayings a city has been raised, gilded, compact and certain, standing on nothing but its own name. Beneath it a faded town sprawls wherever chance set it down. Now and then a street turns and something rare almost shows itself; before you can name it, the old phrases close over it.
motto: Spoken often enough, a city outweighs its own stones.
camera: Distance about 42 from the centre, elevation about 14 degrees, target (0, 6, 0), vertical field of view about 42 degrees, so the ring of letters sits at frame centre with the gilt city above it and the grey sprawl below both in view (the nearest few units of the island rim may crop); slow auto-orbit, one turn per 3 minutes, opposite in direction to the upper city's own rotation so the two visibly slide past each other.
